title: File:Bismuthinite-IMG 9279.jpg
desc: Bismuth is the heaviest of the heavy metals and the only non-toxic one at that. As such, it’s seen a lot of use in replacements for lead, as well as in medications and atomic research.

title: File:Pyrite and bismuthinite (GeoDIL number - 1043).jpg
desc: The dark gray-black mineral is bismuthinite (Bi2S3). Here it is fine grained and massive but it can occur as prismatic to needle like striated crystals or as fibers or foliated sheets. The gold mineral is pyrite (FeS2), commonly called “Fools Gold.” The specimen is 12 cm across.

title: File:Bismuthinite and pyrite (GeoDIL number - 1103).jpg
desc: This sample (6 cm across) contains both bismuthinite and pyrite. Bismuthinite has a steely gray color when fresh, but tarnishes to become yellowish. title: File:Bismuthinite (GeoDIL number - 1105).jpg
desc: The gray semimetallic material is bismuthinite, the gold material is chalcopyrite. Bismuthinite (bismuth sulfide, Bi2S3) is an important ore of bismuth.
